Heritage walk in Leh: the old town, palace and monasteries

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Leh climbs through the old town below the nine-storey Leh Palace (early 17th century) to Namgyal Tsemo, then visits monasteries along the Indus: Shey, Thiksey, Hemis and, further west, Alchi with its 11th to 12th century murals. Leh lies at about 3,500 metres, so groups need two days to acclimatise first.

We arrange Leh and Ladakh study tours on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Leh matters

Leh was the capital of the Ladakhi kingdom of the Namgyal dynasty and a key stop on the caravan routes linking Kashmir, Tibet, Central Asia and Punjab. Pashmina wool, salt, tea, textiles and silver passed through its bazaar, and the town grew around the trade.

It also preserves one of the best-kept Tibetan Buddhist building traditions in India: mud-brick and timber palaces and monasteries, wall paintings, chortens and mani walls. A walk in Leh is a lesson in high-altitude architecture, long-distance trade and Himalayan Buddhism together.

Layers of Leh's history

Ladakh has rock art and petroglyphs along the Indus valley, some of them prehistoric, and the rock art in India guide covers the wider context. Buddhism reached the region early, and the temples of Alchi, painted in about the 11th to 12th century, show strong Kashmiri artistic influence before the later Tibetan style became dominant.

The first Ladakhi dynasty ruled from about the 10th century. The Namgyal dynasty took power in the 15th and 16th centuries, and Sengge Namgyal (ruled in the early 17th century) built Leh Palace and supported Hemis monastery. Tashi Namgyal is credited with the Namgyal Tsemo fort and temple above the palace in the 16th century.

In 1834 the Dogra general Zorawar Singh invaded Ladakh for the Raja of Jammu, and the royal family moved to Stok. Ladakh then became part of Jammu and Kashmir state, and since 2019 it has been a separate Union Territory.

Places a heritage walk in Leh covers

  1. Leh Palace early 17th century

    Nine-storey royal palace of Sengge Namgyal in mud brick and timber, overlooking the town.

  2. Namgyal Tsemo 16th century

    Fort and Gonkhang temple on the peak above the palace, with prayer flags and wide views.

  3. Leh old town 17th century onward

    Mud-brick houses and lanes below the palace, partly restored by conservation projects.

  4. Leh Main Bazaar caravan era onward

    The old trade street where caravans from Kashmir, Tibet and Central Asia arrived.

  5. Jama Masjid, Leh 17th century, rebuilt

    Mosque in the bazaar linked to the Ladakh and Mughal treaty of the 1660s.

  6. Shanti Stupa 1991

    Modern white stupa built with Japanese support, a good viewpoint over the town.

  7. Sankar Gompa 19th century

    Small monastery in Leh town, a branch of Spituk.

  8. Shey Palace 17th century

    Old royal summer palace with a large seated Buddha image, about 15 km from Leh.

  9. Thiksey Monastery 15th century

    Hilltop monastery of the Gelug school, built in tiers up the slope.

  10. Hemis Monastery about 1630

    Large Drukpa monastery founded with the support of Sengge Namgyal, known for its summer festival.

  11. Alchi Choskor about 11th to 12th century

    Temple complex with early murals and painted textiles showing Kashmiri influence.

  12. Stok Palace 1820s

    Residence of the royal family after 1834, with a museum of royal objects.

Walking routes in Leh

Old town and palace on foot

About 3 hours, steep, after acclimatisation

Leh Main Bazaar → Jama Masjid, Leh → Leh old town → Leh Palace → Namgyal Tsemo

The Indus monasteries

Full day, by vehicle

Shey Palace → Thiksey Monastery → Hemis Monastery

Alchi and the west

Full day, by vehicle

Alchi Choskor → Stok Palace

Museums in Leh

  • Central Asian Museum, Leh. Museum in the old town on Leh's caravan trade links with Central Asia, Tibet and Kashmir.
  • Stok Palace Museum. Royal thangkas, jewellery, costumes and objects of the Namgyal family.
  • Hemis Monastery museum. Thangkas, statues and ritual objects held by the monastery.

Best time for a walk

June to September, when roads and flights are reliable. Always plan two days of rest on arrival.

What you see on a walk

In the old town below the palace, students see flat-roofed mud-brick houses, timber beams, narrow lanes and chortens built for a cold desert climate. At Leh Palace, read how a nine-storey building steps up the rock. In the monasteries, look at the assembly hall, the painted walls and the arrangement of images, and treat them as living religious places.

Background on Buddhist sites helps: see Buddhist caves in India, or the lecture Sacred architecture across communities. Students interested in scripts can link Ladakhi inscriptions to India's scripts from Brahmi to Sarada, since Tibetan script derives from a north Indian Brahmi-based model.

Leh for school and college groups

Leh visits are arranged as a study tour built for your group, planned around acclimatisation, travel times and the season. A heritage photography photo walk works especially well in the old town.

Leh is at about 3,500 metres. Groups flying in must rest for at least 36 to 48 hours before any walking, and every student should have a medical check before the trip. The old town, palace and Shanti Stupa are walkable but steep. Shey, Thiksey and Hemis need a vehicle (Hemis is about 45 km away), and Alchi is about 65 km west. Monasteries expect modest dress and quiet behaviour; ask before photographing inside.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Leh?

Leh Palace, Namgyal Tsemo, the old town and bazaar, Shanti Stupa and Sankar Gompa in town, then Shey, Thiksey, Hemis, Stok and Alchi along the Indus valley.

Who built Leh Palace?

Sengge Namgyal, ruler of Ladakh in the early 17th century. The royal family left it after the Dogra invasion of 1834 and moved to Stok.

Is a Leh heritage walk safe for school students?

It can be, with careful planning. Leh is at about 3,500 metres, so students need medical checks, two days of rest before walking, plenty of water and short, slow walks.

Which museums can be visited in Leh?

The Central Asian Museum in the old town, the Stok Palace Museum and the museum at Hemis Monastery.

Can Talaash Heritage arrange a Ladakh study tour?

Yes, on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, planned around altitude and season.
